title: A Lasting Trait, a Past Result

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: The last lesson started in the past and ended now. This one goes the other way. The *si* clause describes something that is true in general: a trait, a habit or a situation that lasts. For that you use the imperfect subjunctive. You know *tuviera* from B1 Unit 4, and *fuera* works the same way: *Si fuera más prudente* means "If he were more careful" (and he is not a careful person). The result clause looks at one thing that happened in the past, so it takes *habría* + participle, as in B1 Unit 35: *Si fuera más prudente, no habría dicho eso* means "If he were more careful, he would not have said that." The imperfect subjunctive here does not point to the past. It pictures a lasting quality that is not true, and the second clause says what that quality cost us back then.

sections.title: Which clause looks where?
rows: Si hubiera estudiado medicina, ahora sería médica.
Last lesson: a past condition, a result now.
Si fuera más paciente, habría esperado.
This lesson: a lasting trait, a past result.
Si fuera más prudente, no habría dicho eso.
If he were more careful, he would not have said that.
Si hablara mejor inglés, habría conseguido el puesto.
If I spoke better English, I would have got the job.

items.spanish: Si mi hermano no fuera tan terco, habría pedido perdón.
items.english: If my brother were not so stubborn, he would have said sorry.

items.spanish: Si no tuviéramos miedo a volar, habríamos ido en avión.
items.english: If we were not afraid of flying, we would have gone by plane.

items.spanish: Si Marta fuera más ordenada, no habría perdido las llaves.
items.english: If Marta were tidier, she would not have lost the keys.

items.spanish: Si mi hermana viviera cerca, la habríamos visitado más.
items.english: If my sister lived nearby, we would have visited her more.

sections.content: Ask yourself whether the condition is one moment or a lasting quality. For one moment in the past, use the full past pattern: *Si hubiera estado cansado ayer, no habría salido*. For a trait or a situation (*ser*, *tener*, *vivir*, *hablar*), use the imperfect subjunctive: *Si fuera más prudente…*. In the result you can also use *hubiera* + participle instead of *habría*, as you saw in B2 Unit 10: *Si fuera más prudente, no hubiera dicho eso*.
